PHBR1 p.116. A stick a few feet long with a broad, shallow groove running its length and a knot at the end. The character rests a javelin's butt against the knot with the shaft lying along the groove, holds it at the other end, and uses the atl-atl as a LEVER to throw much farther than by hand. WORKS ONLY WITH A JAVELIN -- not a spear, long spear, harpoon or trident. Used with one, the javelin's missile line becomes ROF 2/3, S 3, M 6, L 9. Can be carved out of a stick by anyone with the Weaponsmithing proficiency.

PHBR1 p.117. A mechanical sheath worn on the forearm just below the elbow, for ONE of Dagger, Knife or Stiletto -- a sheath for one of the three will not hold either of the other two, and it cannot be built for any other weapon. Straightening and flexing the arm pops the blade into the hand; the character makes a Dexterity check at +3 to catch it, and a natural 20 always fails. On a failure the blade pops straight out and drops to the floor -- it cannot be 'shot out' as a thrown attack, will not hurt whoever it hits, and always hits hilt-first when fumbled. The wearer must ANNOUNCE BEFORE INITIATIVE is rolled that he intends to pop the blade; when his action comes up he may still attack that round, since arming himself does not use up an attack. Requires someone with BOTH the Set Snares and Weaponsmithing proficiencies to create. Like the Spring-Out Spike it is illegal in most places, but a lesser crime: a fine of 10d6 gp and 1d6 days in jail.

PHBR1 pp.116-117. A blade identical in characteristics to the KNIFE, housed in an innocuous rod or handle; pressing the secret catch snaps the blade out and the character is instantly armed. Usually built into something the character will be carrying anyway and would not wish known to be a weapon -- the ends of quarterstaves (which converts a staff into a spear), sometimes the hilts of swords and daggers. Assassins often carry a dagger with an ordinary blade and a poison-coated spring-out spike. MUST BE BUILT IN WHEN THE ITEM IS FIRST CREATED and cannot customarily be added to an existing weapon; built into an ordinary object it adds 1 lb and 40 gp to that object's cost. ILLEGAL in most civilizations -- authorities who catch a character using one will jail him on the assumption of assassination motives.
